name: Blaze King
research_notes: SITE: blazeking.com (WordPress/WooCommerce). Product slugs often do not match model names: /ashford-30/ = Ashford 30.2, /chinook-30/ = Chinook 30.2, /sirocco-20/ = Sirocco 20.2, /sirocco-30/ = Sirocco 30.2, /king-classic/ = King 40, /princess-classic/ = Princess 32 (PE32), /princess-insert/ = Princess 29. LINEUP: Wood Free Standing lists 9 stoves and Wood Inserts lists 3; all 12 are in this batch, so missing_from_catalog is empty. Chinook 20.2 is the only discontinued record (old product URL 404s; manual moved to Archived Manuals; dropped from the 09-2026 20 Series brochure). GAS: the site menu still shows Gas Free Standing, Gas Fireplaces and Gas Inserts, but all three category pages say 'No products were found matching your selection'. Gas PDFs still turn up in site search: Clarity CL2714 gas insert brochure (10-2023), CL2714.IPI manual (v2.01, Sep 2023), Clarity CL26 SP/IPI manuals (2022), plus legacy gas manuals. They were not read. No current gas product pages were found. Out of scope for this batch either way. SYSTEMIC CONFLICT (page vs PDF): for the 20 Series, 30 Series, Boxer 24, Princess 32 and the 25-size inserts, product pages show higher heat outputs and slightly larger firebox volumes than the 09-2026 brochures, which cite 'per 2024 test report' or 'EPA listed' figures. Example: Sirocco/Ashford 20.2 page 32,776/11,370 BTU/h vs brochure 31,092/10,786. Per spec, normalized values use the product page; brochure values are in specs_raw and notes. King 40 and Princess 29 pages agree with their brochures. BTU CONVENTION: Blaze King publishes 'Constant Heat Output' high/low with durations (e.g. '32,776 BTU's/h for up to 8 hours'). btu_output_max/min take those numbers; the durations stay in specs_raw. Sentry S14 publishes no durations. EFFICIENCY: the Efficiency & Emissions page labels all figures 'HHV Tested Efficiency', so efficiency_basis = HHV. COMBUSTION: every model is catalytic (thermostat plus catalytic combustor, 10-year combustor warranty). For Sentry S14 this rests on its brochure's combustor warranty only; confirm with the S14 manual. EPA: '2020 certified' wording was confirmed only in the AF20.2 manual. Other records use the wording their sources publish: 'EPA listed' (20 Series, King/Princess, Boxer and insert brochures) or 'EPA certified' (EPA seal on the Ashford 30.2 page). It is null for Chinook 30.2, Sirocco 30.2 and Sentry S14, where no EPA wording was found in the sources read. Most current-model manuals could not be read, so their exact certification wording is unconfirmed. NOT READ: the WebFetch proxy returned HTTP 429 for 180-CK20.2-v3.01, 180-AF30.2-v2.51, 180-CK30.2-v3.01, 180-SC30.2-v3.01, 180-KE40-v3.01, 180-PE32-v3.01, 180-BX24-v2.51 and 180-S14, so they were not retried. The AF20.2 'Appliance Dimensions' PDF returned no text (image-only drawing), so the other dimension PDFs were not tried. Overall height/width/depth are therefore null except Sentry S14 height. IMAGES: no product image on the site has alt text, so alt is null. Pixel sizes are not shown (null). Variants and roles are inferred from file names (e.g. _Room = lifestyle, _Product = cutout); spot-check roles where marked 'other'. DOCUMENTS: manuals are combined 'Operation & Installation' manuals (confirmed for AF20.2) and are typed installation_manual. 'Installation Clearances' PDFs are manual excerpts (typed other). The AF20.2 manual says French manuals are on the website, but no French links were seen. Older-generation manuals (e.g. SC20, CK30, AF30 v1, AF20.1) are in the Archived Manuals section and are mentioned in notes, not attached. Superseded brochure editions and an older manual revision seen in search results are attached and marked 'not read'.

No HTTP 429 this pass: every manual, page and architect guide that pass 1 could not load was read, so no retries were needed. MENDOTA: the manuals have a dotted-leader ratings block (model no., 'P.4 fireplace efficiency', flue venting, SAFETY/ignition, blowers, net weight, framing); their P.4 figures differ slightly from the pages' CSA P.4.1 values (page kept). DXV60 is a manual-spark thermocouple/thermopile unit (standing pilot). DXV45 and FV41 Arch are PF2 IPI with a CPI mode, recorded as 'IPI/CPI selectable'; pass-1 sibling records list this same system as 'IPI', so harmonize if wanted. The ML-Series manual mentions no CPI mode. MORSO: efficiency and emissions now come from the NA manuals (6100 B, 7110 C, 5660 B Standard). The 2025 US/CA catalog PDF (form 72780500) was added for 7 Morso records; it still prints old 7110 figures under the name '7110 B'. The 1410 B and 1440 B US pages still have one image each; the UK 1410 page is a discontinued 1984-1990 model, and the UK 1412 page is a different model, so neither was used. SAFETY: the 5660 B Standard NA manual says 'Do NOT install in a mobile home' while the page says Yes (US only). MAJESTIC: the Rev C Echelon manual 2608-980 rev Z and all six architect guides were read; both Echelon records have full per-size sizes[]. Shared Hearth & Home option tiles (remotes, swatches, icons, Mezzo/Marquis images) were skipped. BLAZE KING: the S14 manual confirms catalytic.

name: Kozy Heat
research_notes: RATE LIMITING: partway through, the WebFetch proxy returned HTTP 429 for kozyheat.com and said not to retry. Five product pages were never read: generation-6020, nordik-36dv, nordik-41dv, nordik-48dv and nordik-48tl. Those records were built from official Kozy Heat brochures and installation manuals found by site search, plus the current gas fireplaces category page (for status, URL and a 400x285 thumbnail). They need a revisit for gallery images and their full linked-document lists. The resources page (kozyheat.com/resources/) lists those documents by name, but the extractor would not return their URLs. Later fetches were spaced about 30 s apart and succeeded. UNIT AND FIELD CONVENTIONS: Kozy Heat publishes gas input ('BTU/hr Input', NG and LP). Product pages often give only the high figure; series brochures give High/Low, mapped to btu_input_*_max/min. Where one record covers versions with different low-fire figures (Bayport IPI vs millivolt), *_min is left null and per-version values are in specs_raw. Kozy Heat publishes three NG/LP efficiency pairs: EnerGuide P.4, Steady State and AFUE. P.4 and steady state are in specs_raw. Product pages do not publish dimensions, weight or vent size, so those come from the series brochures. VIEW AREA ORDER: product pages are inconsistent. Callaway 50, Callaway See-Thru, SP34, SP41 and Springfield 36 pages list height first; the brochures list width first. For SP34, SP41 and Springfield 36 the brochure numbers are also slightly larger than the page's. view_area is recorded exactly as each product page publishes it. PAGE VS BROCHURE CONFLICTS (product page used, details in record notes): Bellingham 44 LP low, Callaway 50 NG low and LP high, Callaway 72 LP, Bayport 41 millivolt BTU and P.4, and SP34/SP41/Springfield view areas. Nordik 36DV vent: the brochure prints '4 x 6' but the manual says 4 x 6-5/8 co-axial (manual used). IMAGES: product pages show only room scenes (mostly 1024 px '-e<timestamp>' crops, plus some full-size originals) with almost no alt text. No white-background cutouts were seen anywhere, so no primary_cutout is assigned. Variants are inferred from file names. Shared accessory PDFs (heat transfer kits, KPV power vent, Komfort Zone Kits, vinyl addendum, log-set instructions) are typed 'other'. Bilingual PDFs use language 'en/fr'. All values come from a summarizing extractor; key rows were re-asked verbatim.

Site: kozyheat.com (WordPress). Each product page has a spec table plus links to a category brochure. Brochures read: Gas Insert Brochure (printed 6-14-24; covers Chaska 25/29/335S/34 and Nordik 29i/34i), Freestanding brochure (Lakefield XL, Oakport), Osseo eSeries brochure (code 6-26; e29/e34/e50/e64/e80) and Osseo X brochure (X50/X64). Efficiency: Kozy Heat publishes EnerGuide P.4, steady-state and AFUE figures for NG and LP. The normalized efficiency_ng_pct/efficiency_lp_pct use AFUE; P.4 and steady state are in specs_raw. Inputs: product pages give max input; low/turndown inputs come from the brochures. Dimensions: insert and electric brochures use lettered diagrams (A-K / A-H) with no legend in the extracted text, so height/width/depth are null for those; the stoves have labelled H/W/D. Product-page view areas often differ slightly from the brochure (Chaska 25/29/335S/34, Oakport, Osseo e34, Osseo X64). Page values are used and both are noted. sizes[] holds versions rather than sizes for Chaska 29 (Log/Rock, Glass, MV), Lakefield XL (IPI/MV) and Oakport 18 (IPI/MV), and true sizes for the two Osseo eSeries families. Electric output '750W / 1500W @ 120V | 5,000' is mapped to electric_watts_max 1500 / electric_btu_max 5000. Kozy Heat publishes no heating area, certification or warranty for the electric units. Rate-limited (HTTP 429, not retried): /product/chaska-29-glass/ and /product/chaska-34-log/. These are uncategorized version pages (listed as ':: Select Product Type'), along with /product/chaska-29-log/ and /product/chaska-34-glass/ (not fetched); they are not treated as separate models. The '?product_type=direct_vent' filter page lists every product, including electric ones, so it is not evidence of venting type. The Electric Fireplaces category now lists 'Osseo X Series' (X50 + X64) instead of the X64 page, but /product/osseo-x64/ is still live. FYI for the kozy-heat-fireplaces batch: the full listing also shows Bayport 36 Traditional Log, Bayport 41 Traditional Log and Generation 7220 (Gas Fireplaces). These are outside this batch's categories and not added to missing_from_catalog.

No HTTP 429 this pass; fetches ran one at a time. WORDPRESS MEDIA ENDPOINT: Kozy Heat's 'product' post type is not in the REST API, so /wp-json/wp/v2/media?search= lists only uploads not attached to a product. It returns at most 10 items per page (page 2+ needs per_page=10, else HTTP 400), but it still surfaced full-size, model-named photos not shown on the current product pages (Bayport 41, Springfield 36, Callaway 50/72, Chaska 25/29/34/335S, Nordik 34i); those are recorded with the endpoint URL as source_page. NO CUTOUTS: no white-background cutouts or dimension drawings were found for any model; galleries are room scenes and some screenshots. Image content can't be viewed through the fetch tool, so roles come from file names. URL ENCODING: four on-file screenshot URLs (Nordik 48TL, Nordik 60TL, Osseo eSeries Inserts x2) use a plain space where the real file names have U+202F and return 404; working %E2%80%AF versions are added and the broken ones should be dropped (not put in images_remove, since they are the right model). INSTALLATION SPECS: Kozy Heat's Sell Sheets page needs a dealer login, but its 'Installation Specs' PDFs are public uploads listed by the media endpoint; the newest sheet per current model is added as spec_sheet (EN/FR). These sheets separate actual and framing sizes. That gave insert height/width/depth for Chaska 25/29/34/335S and Nordik 29i/34i, and shows the Callaway 40/50/72 brochure 'Depth 22' equals the framing depth (actual 18-15/16), which is flagged and not changed. HEATING AREA: not published on any Kozy Heat page, brochure or sheet read; it stays null for all 30. Lakefield XL and Osseo X64 are omitted (their pages show nothing new). Pass 1's 'Bayport 36 Glass' candidate appears to be the Bayport 36's own glass version (BAY-36-G manual).

browse.sorts_by: By product type (gas fireplaces, gas inserts, gas stoves), with a fire-material filter: Rock, Glass, Log, Wood. No shape groups; some model pages name the shape (Bellingham: landscape; Callaway: linear; Nordik TL: tall linear).

name: Jøtul
research_notes: Site layout: jotul.com moved to a new Next.js site. Old product links (/products/gas-stoves/<slug>) still serve the legacy page (which carries efficiency and heat-input lines) for GF 160 DV, GF 160 DV IPI, GF 200 DV II, GF 300 DV IPI, GF 370 DV, GF 400 DV and GF 500 DV IPI; the others land on the new US pages; the GF 370 DV IPI old product link returns 404. product_url is the current /us/ page for every record. Current product pages are /us/products/gas-stoves/jotul-<slug> and show only weight, height, width, depth, heating capacity and flue exit – no BTU, efficiency, ignition or document links (their 'Technical data' / 'Technical documentation' sections were empty in every fetch). The new site is fed by a public Sanity CMS dataset (project 7yge4kng, the same source as the cdn.sanity.io images); I queried it read-only via its HTTP query API to get each model's full technical data, finish variants, image list and document links. Those are cited as 'site product data' (query URLs in sources). Documents are served from documents.jotulgroup.com (Jøtul's own document host); most legacy /sites/usa/files/ PDF links 404. Manuals were read for all 16 models; BTU figures in specs are gas INPUT ratings (Jøtul publishes no BTU output for these stoves). Efficiency: Jøtul publishes steady-state, AFUE and CSA P.4.1-15 figures; the normalized efficiency_ng/lp_pct fields hold the CSA P.4.1-15 values (all three in specs_raw). Images: product galleries alternate 1000x1000 transparent finish cutouts (alt '<model> <finish code>') with room/plain-background photos; cutout vs photo roles come from the CMS image metadata (hasAlpha) and blurhash previews, since image content cannot be fetched – a human should spot-check roles. Several galleries include images belonging to other models (noted per record and excluded). Listing-card images that never appear on a product page were not recorded. Document language 'en/fr' = one parts-diagram file Jøtul lists for both its English and French-Canadian sites. Finish codes (matched to legacy-page colour names): MB Matte Black, BP Black Paint, BB Blue Black enamel, BRM Brown Majolica enamel, LI Linen enamel; WH appears only on unpublished variants. Pages not read: https://www.jotul.com/products/gas-stoves/gf-300-bv-allagash/manuals (HTTP 429 rate limit); the flippingbook gas brochure (not machine-readable); the planning guide's per-model spec tables were only partially extractable. Also read for context: https://www.jotul.com/us/manuals (lists wood products only in the visible portion) and https://www.jotul.com/us/brochure. missing_from_catalog is empty: the site's product data lists exactly these 16 current (Published) US/CA gas stoves; the only other North American gas stove there, GF 200 DV IPI Lillehammer, is marked Discontinued.

SITE: Old product links (jotul.com/products/<cat>/<slug>) mostly redirect to canonical US pages (jotul.com/us/products/wood-stoves|wood-fireplace-inserts|gas-fireplace-inserts/jotul-<slug>). Short links for F 445 Holliday CF and F 602 V3 returned empty pages on at least one fetch. The canonical US pages give WebFetch only six key specs: weight, H/W/D, 'Max Output (kW)' (wood) or 'Flue Exit Options' (gas), and heating capacity. The full 'Technical data' table, 'Technical documentation' (manual PDFs) and colour names are not in the HTML WebFetch receives. UNITS: 'Max Output' carries a kW unit label, but the values are BTU/hr-scale (55000–70000). F 35 '59.443', F 602 V3 '37.5' and the C 550 V2 CF heating capacity '1.7' look like European thousands-separator errors. None of these is normalized; Efficiency is published as both LHV and HHV; HHV is used as the headline. DOCUMENTS: EPA report PDFs (cdn.sanity.io/files/fgd08pi3/...) are linked from jotul.com/us/epa-certifications. WebFetch can't read them: robots.txt disallowed one, and the proxy returned HTTP 429 on a second, with instructions not to retry. Their URLs are recorded as epa_report documents. Brochures (2025 Gas Brochure, 2025 wood brochure) are FlippingBook flipbooks with no readable content and no PDF link. The manuals hub (jotul.com/us/manuals) lists products with 'View Documents' buttons whose targets aren't exposed, so no installation/owner's manual URL was captured for any model, including GI 635. IMAGES: roles were inferred from file type, dimensions and alt text only; no images were viewed. A square 1000x1000 PNG with a finish code is treated as a finish cutout, and one is kept per finish; primary_cutout is the first such PNG on the page. Large (3000 px) landscape JPGs are treated as lifestyle. The hero image whose alt text is the bare model name (a 1000x1000 JPG, or on the C 550 an 831x872 PNG) and all non-square PNGs are marked 'other' because they may be product-on-background shots, angled cutouts or benefit illustrations. A human should check these. EPA reports are attached only where the EPA page's model name matches the record; CF variants carry the base model's report URL in notes. FINISH CODES: BP = Black paint and LI = Linen (F 500 V3 Oslo CF colour list); MB = Matte black (F 35). I, BRO and BB are not spelled out. UNREADABLE: jotul.com/us/products?productType=WoodStoves returned HTTP 500. The /us/products/wood-stoves listing was used instead. LINEUP: the US category pages list wood stoves (F 35, F 445, F 445 CF, F 500 V3 Oslo, F 500 V3 Oslo CF, F 602 V3), wood inserts (C 550 V2 Rockland, C 550 V2 Rockland CF) and gas inserts (GI 535, GI 545, GI 635, GI 645). The EPA page also lists EPA 2020 reports for F 445 V2 Holliday, F 45 V2 Greenville and F 55 V2 Carrabassett, which have no US product listing. They are not added to missing_from_catalog.

SOURCES: jotul.com is fed by a public Sanity dataset (project 7yge4kng). Its read-only HTTP query API was used per product for technicalSpecifications, document links and variant image lists (query URLs are in each record's sources). WebFetch's proxy rejects URLs longer than ~220 characters, so queries were kept short and one product at a time. Every manual, EPA report and planning guide was read from documents.jotulgroup.com. EPA DATABASE: cfpub.epa.gov's robots.txt disallows all agents (User-agent: * / Disallow: /, ClaudeBot included), and the search-results URL returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, so the EPA database was not read. Wood figures come from Jøtul's manuals and from the EPA certification test reports Jøtul hosts on documents.jotulgroup.com (F 35, F 445, F 500 V3). Those documents.jotulgroup.com report copies are added as epa_report documents next to the cdn.sanity.io copies already on file; they are probably the same reports, but the cdn.sanity.io/files PDFs are robots-blocked, so the F 602 V3 and C 550 V2 reports are still unread. WOOD OUTPUT MAPPING: btu_output_min/max = Jøtul's printed 'Heat Output Range', which the manuals footnote as measured in the EPA emissions tests. Jøtul's separate 'Max. Heat Output' (a more frequent refuelling cycle than the EPA high-burn test) goes to btu_output_cordwood_max as the peak figure, only where the page's 'Max Output' agrees (F 445 55,000; F 500 V3 70,000). The page's 'Max Output (kW)' is really BTU/hr: F 35 '59.443' = 59,443. On the C 550 V2 CF (65000 vs manual 36,214) and the F 602 V3 (37.5 vs planning guide 28,000) it conflicts with the PDFs and is not normalized. 'CF' = Clean Face: the F 445 and F 500 V3 manuals cover 'Classic and Clean Face Models', and the C 550 V2 manual covers Clean Face and Traditional Lattice styles of one insert. The manuals and EPA reports call the F 445, F 500 V3, F 602 V3 and C 550 V2 catalytic (the pages market 'non-catalytic technology' plus the High Flow combustor); the F 35 is non-catalytic. The 2025 Wood Product Planning Guide has no date or revision and disagrees with pages and manuals in places (F 500 V3 2,000 sq ft and 9 h; F 35 59,433 BTU/hr and 365 lb), so it is used only as a cross-check. GALLERIES: the site-data variant image lists of all 17 records were compared with what is on file. New images exist only for the C 550 V2 CF (1), GI 535 (11), GI 545 (4) and GI 645 (3). All are transparent 1000x1000 PNGs shown on the product pages with '<model> <finish code>' alt text, and each URL was verified against the asset store. The extra same-finish cutouts are not labelled by option. The gas-insert bullets list cast-iron vs rectangle/arched steel overlays and media choices, which probably explains them, but a human may want to prune them. Product-level listing cutouts that never appear on the product pages (F 35 6c007aeb…, F 445 07c8427b…) were not recorded, matching the first pass. No dimension-drawing images are published (drawings exist only inside the manuals). The wood-stove galleries and the six gas-stove galleries (GF 200 DV II, GF 305, GF 500 x2, GF 520 x2) have nothing beyond what is on file, so GF 200, GF 305 and both GF 520 records are omitted. LINEUP: the site data's published US wood stoves, wood inserts, gas inserts and gas stoves match the catalog (plus the C 550 V2 Rockland non-CF the first pass already reported). jotul.com/us/epa-certifications now also lists 'Jøtul F 45 V3 Holliday' (EPA 2020), which has no product in the site data. No HTTP 429 responses were met in this pass.

browse.sorts_by: Gas inserts are one list with no groups; Jøtul describes the range as running from traditional to contemporary.

name: Pacific Energy
research_notes: Pacific Energy (pacificenergy.net, WordPress). Wood spec tables label 'Heat Output (Cord Wood)' -> btu_output_cordwood_max and 'Heat Output (EPA Test Fuel)' -> btu_output_epa. Where PE's EPA report for the model was read, its burn-rate heat-output range is in btu_output_min/max. EFFICIENCY BASIS IS NOT UNIFORM: inserts and the FP25 / FP25 Arch pages say 'Efficiency (HHV)', but the FP16, FP16 Arch, FP30 and FP30 Arch pages say 'Efficiency (LHV)' (68% / 76.8%). PE's FP30 EPA report gives 69% HHV / 73% LHV, which supports neither 76.8% reading; flagged for review. Gas efficiencies are CSA P.4.1-15 (efficiency_basis 'P.4.1'). Product pages give no dimensions, heating area or flue size for the wood units. Heating area and approximate burn time come from PE brochures (2025 Wood Burning Inserts LE2 11900081; 2022 Wood Inserts 11900070 for models not in the 2025 edition; Wood Fireplaces LE 11900072, 06/22) and are attributed in specs_raw. Where a brochure gives a burn-time range (e.g. 7-10 h), burn_time_hr_max holds the upper value. The brochures use a multi-column layout and WebFetch sometimes put values under the wrong model. Values that disagreed with the product page were not used, and the 2022 brochures in particular conflict with current pages (e.g. FP16 cord wood 56,000 vs 70,000; FP30 EPA output 41,275 vs 65,650; Summit firebox 3.0 vs 2.5). Product-page values are used throughout. Gas: ignition, vent size, minimum inputs and certification came from the installation manuals (all four gas families use SIT Proflame 2 with selectable IPI/CPI). Unit dimensions are recorded only for the Trenton (manual) and the Esprit L44 height/width (brochure). Tofino z25 dimensions conflict across sources and are left null. AVAILABILITY: the FP30 LE and FP30 Arch LE pages say 'TEMPORARILY UNAVAILABLE IN THE UNITED STATES'. Status is 'current' with this flagged. Category pages: the Wood Inserts page lists exactly the 10 inserts in this batch; Wood Fireplaces lists exactly the 6 FP records. The gas category pages (gas-fireplaces, gas-stoves, gas-inserts) render no product list to the fetcher (gas-inserts shows 'Please select listing to show'). The Manuals and Brochures pages list exactly Trenton/Trenton Classic, Esprit L44 and z25 Premium/Standard as gas products. No missing models were found in these categories. Two LE2 inserts (Neo 1.6 Insert LE2, Vista Insert LE2) publish 23,200 BTU EPA output, the same as the LE versions, but PE's own certification report for them gives 12,315-30,149 BTU/hr. The page figure is kept and flagged. Rate limiting: the WebFetch proxy returned HTTP 429 on second reads of the Alderlea T5 Insert LE page, the Neo 1.6 Insert LE page and the 2025 insert brochure. Data comes from the first successful read of each. venting='chimney' for wood inserts and wood fireplaces (they vent into a masonry or listed factory-built chimney, usually with a liner for inserts; not re-verified in the manuals). flue_diameter_in (6 in.) comes from the product page (Neo 1.6 Insert LE2, Vista Insert LE2), PE's EPA reports (FP16, FP25 and FP30 families) or the insert brochures, where every extraction of both editions gave 6 in. for every insert.

SITE: pacificenergy.net is WordPress/Elementor. A plain WebFetch of a product page drops every link and image, so I used a structured prompt that asks for links and images in separate parts. The REST API returns product titles and status tags but no spec content. Query-string URLs are blocked by robots.txt. Every product page has a 'You might also like' strip of other models (mostly NeoViews); those images and their manual links were not recorded. EPA badges, 'design a fire' icons and generic enamel colour chips were skipped. Door, leg and trivet finish photos were kept as 'detail' where the page showed them. Room-installation photos (og:image, 1400x700) came from products-sitemap.xml. BLOCKED: three product pages were refused by the fetch proxy (HTTP 429, told not to retry): Neo 2.5 LE (/products/neo-25le-wood-stove/), Neo 2.5 LE2 (/products/neo-2-5-le2/) and NeoView 2.5 LE (/products/neoview-25-le/). Those three records rely on Pacific Energy brochures, manuals, EPA reports and the listing pages. CONVENTIONS: 'Cord Wood' (NeoView 2.5 LE2: 'Peak Output (Cordwood)') maps to btu_output_cordwood_max and 'EPA Test Fuel' to btu_output_epa; efficiency is HHV throughout. btu_output_min/max hold the manual or EPA-report tested range only where I read it. Dimensions were left null everywhere because the brochure dimension drawings came back inconsistently. Specs come from the product page; brochure values fill gaps (heating area, burn time, flue, viewing dimensions), and page/brochure conflicts are in each record's notes. US MARKET: every readable first-generation LE stove page says 'NOT FOR SALE IN THE USA' (13 pages): Alderlea T4 LE, T4 Classic LE, T5 LE, T5 Classic LE, T6 LE, Neo 1.6 LE, Summit LE, Summit Classic LE, Super LE, Super Classic LE, SuperLE 27HD, Vista LE and Vista Classic LE. For T5 LE, T6 LE and Vista Classic LE my first read was an older copy without the notice, and a same-day re-check showed it. The Neo 2.5 LE and NeoView 2.5 LE pages were unreadable. The NeoView 2.5 LE manual is NON-EPA and certified for Canada only. Pacific Energy moved the US editions of Alderlea T4 LE, Neo 1.6 LE, Neo 2.5 LE and Vista LE to Discontinued Products on 2025-12-05. Those four are set to 'unclear', because the US edition is discontinued while the non-US page stays live. The other notice-bearing models stay 'current' (live page and current lineup, but not sold in the US). Every first-generation LE stove page was edited on 2026-10-06 (products-sitemap lastmod), the day before this check, so the notices look new. A Wisconsin dealer should confirm US availability with the distributor before listing any LE (first-generation) model. No LE2 page carries a restriction. Neo 1.6 LE2 has the site's 'Pre-Order LE2' status tag. It comes from a cordwood EPA test whose high-fire run was 59,861 Btu/hr, so it is not a mislabel. However, the LE2 brochure 11900083 still prints 60,000, so btu_output_epa for Neo 2.5 LE2 is left null. LE and LE2 are distinct throughout: separate pages, specs, manuals and EPA reports. EPA reports are shared across models: Vista LE report (T4 LE, T4 Classic LE, Neo 1.6 LE, Vista LE, Vista Classic LE), NEO 1.6 LE2 report (T4 LE2, T4 Classic LE2, Neo 1.6 LE2, Vista LE2, Vista Classic LE2), Super LE report (T5 LE, T5 Classic LE, Super LE, Super Classic LE, SuperLE 27HD), Summit LE report (T6 LE, Summit LE, Summit Classic LE), Neo 2.5 LE report and NEO 2.5 LE2 report. NAMING: Pacific Energy's product title is 'Super<sup>LE</sup> 27HD', i.e. SuperLE 27HD. The page heading, listing, manuals index and EPA index use that form. name: RSF
research_notes: SITES: icc-rsf.com hosts both RSF and Renaissance. Its fireplace menu lists exactly the 9 RSF and 4 Renaissance models in this batch. wilkeningfireplace.com lists 2 fireplaces (both in this batch) plus sealed fireplace doors (Grand Seal, FullView, Supreme). The doors are not fireplaces, so they are not listed as missing; Wilkening's archived brochures (Intens a Fyre, Magna Fyre, Ultra Great) are discontinued. missing_from_catalog is empty. RSF CONVENTIONS: 'BTU Output' is the EPA crib-wood test figure (btu_output_epa); 'BTU Maximum' / 'Estimated BTU Potential' is an RSF engineering estimate (btu_output_max). efficiency_pct is RSF 'Optimal Efficiency' (LHV); the EPA average (HHV) figure is in specs_raw. RSF weights are shipping/crated weights. RSF publishes one manual per model, labelled 'Owner's Manual' (file prefix RSF-II...). It is typed owners_manual, but it probably also holds the installation instructions; check before filing it in the installation-manual store. The RSF 2025-06 catalog (Brochure_RSF_EN_2025_06_WEB.pdf) gives slightly different outside dimensions from the product pages for the Focus 3600B, the Pearl 3600B (height 38 11/16 vs 43 3/4 in) and the Opel Keystone; the page values are used and the differences are noted. The Focus 320 is Canada-only and EPA 2015 Step 1 and is absent from that catalog. RENAISSANCE CONVENTIONS: these are fireplaces not regulated under EPA NSPS Subpart AAA. Emissions are published in g/kg with the door open and closed; emissions_g_kg holds the door-open (worst-case) figure and door-closed is in specs_raw. The 2023-2024 Renaissance catalog's Rumford figures ('1000B/1500B') differ from the product pages on weight and log length (Rumford 1500: 1,085 vs 851 lb). The current 2025 manuals are filed as RR1000C/RR1500C, so the catalog may predate a revision; the page values are used. install_type zero_clearance comes from the catalog's 0-inch back/side/floor clearances and its ULC S-610/UL127 listing. WILKENING: specs are on the product pages and brochures; all manuals and brochures are on the central Downloads page. IMAGES: roles are inferred from page section, filename and alt text, not visually checked. Only the Opel Plus Keystone has white-background cutouts. Accessory-only images (blowers, vent kits, gaskets, louvers) and logos/badges are excluded. FETCH ISSUES: one targeted re-fetch of https://icc-rsf.com/fireplace/rsf/pearl-3600/ (to quote BTU footnotes) was refused with HTTP 429 (rate limited). The first read of that page was complete, so no data is missing.

name: Kuma
about: Kuma Stoves is a family-run US maker (wood stoves since 1981) of hand-fabricated hybrid wood stoves and masonry-only wood inserts (burn tubes plus a catalytic combustor), plus the Applewood wood cook stove and Snow Destroyer roof snow dividers, sold through US dealers with online ordering offered where no dealer is nearby. The current 'LE-1' models replaced same-named 2020 'LE' versions (different manuals and listing tags, so match the manual to the tag), and the 2015-era Aspen, Tamarack, Ashwood, Wood Classic and Sequoia stoves and inserts and the Arctic and Oil Classic oil stoves are discontinued.
research_notes: LINEUP: Kuma's current Wood Stoves page lists six LE-1 stoves (Aspen, Tamarack, Aberdeen on the 1.8 cu ft K-181 firebox; Ashwood, Wood Classic, Cambridge on the 2.5 cu ft K-251 firebox) plus the Applewood cook stove. The Wood Inserts page lists the Alpine LE-1 (K-181) and Cascade LE-1 (K-251). All 8 LE-1 product pages are live, show 'Available' and an item number (K-xxx-LE-1). Each model has one product page and no size variants, so sizes[] is empty. The Applewood went to missing_from_catalog as a cook stove; move it into records if Stoveworks wants cook stoves under wood stoves. EXCLUDED (not for sale): both category pages link an 'older line' page (/Content/Page/wood-stoves-older, /wood-inserts-older) listing the Aspen, Tamarack, Ashwood, Wood Classic and Sequoia stoves and the Aspen, Ashwood and Sequoia inserts. Every one of those product pages is headed '<name> (Discontinued)' (all 8 checked). The Manuals page files the 2020 'LE' versions (K-180/K-250: Aspen LE ... Cascade LE) under 'Out Of Production Models'. Oil stoves (Arctic, Oil Classic) are also '(Discontinued)'. The Shasta oil stove and the Platinum SE pellet grill appear only as manuals, so none of these is listed. SITE: product URLs are /Store/ProductDetails/<slug>, and the LE-1 slugs drop the '-1' (aspen-le = Aspen LE-1). Images and PDFs are on kumastorage.blob.core.windows.net. No HTTP 429s or blocked pages. SPEC CONVENTIONS: each page prints "Cordwood BTU's 63,000 (29,153 EPA est.)", mapped to btu_output_cordwood_max and btu_output_epa. btu_output_min/max come from the EPA range printed in the manuals (K-181 12,764-29,153; K-251 11,219-30,612 Btu/hr), as in the Pacific Energy batch. Pages print both 78% HHV and 84% LHV; HHV is used (the K-251 manuals say 77.8%). combustion_type 'hybrid' comes from the manuals and brochures (burn tubes plus an Applied Catalysts ACI-5M combustor); the product pages mention it only in customer reviews. LOG LENGTH: pages print an unqualified 'Wood Length' (16 or 18 in), and the manuals call it the 'recommended wood length' without giving a maximum. It is stored as log_length_recommended_in, log_length_max_in is null, so merge.py's log-length headline will be blank. Map it to max if preferred. Stove heights use the base configuration (steel legs, or no lower platform); the pedestal or platform height is in specs_raw. SYSTEMIC PAGE-VS-BROCHURE CONFLICTS (stoves only; the rev. 260211 brochures; page values used): heating capacity, page 1,800 / 2,800 sq ft vs brochure 1,400-2,000 / 2,400-3,000; weights, page 365-470 lb vs brochure 400-565 lb, always higher (Cambridge 470 vs 565). For the inserts, page and brochure agree. The brochures' dimension figures sit on unlabeled drawings, so they were not used, and the manuals' drawings are not machine-readable. Clearances come from the brochure tables. Other flags: Wood Classic depth 26-1/8 in (equals its width) and the Cascade brochure footnote that repeats the Alpine output figures; see record notes. IMAGES: never viewed. The PNG configuration shots (e.g. ASP_BLK_LGSB.png = black, steel legs) are cutouts, with the base configuration as primary_cutout. The '2026 Brochure <model>.jpg' main photos are role 'other' (they may be room scenes). Kuma's gallery alt text ends with a 'Total price as shown' sentence giving a dollar amount, which was removed under the no-prices rule. DOCUMENTS: each product page's 'Owner's Manual' link is titled 'Installation and Operating Instructions' and includes installation steps and a parts list, so it is typed installation_manual. Listing tags, blower instructions and the site-wide biomass tax-credit certificates are typed 'other'. EPA test reports are linked but were not opened. TAX CREDIT: Kuma's EPA page marks every LE-1 model as qualifying 'YES (before 01/01/2026)' only. The site still links a '2025 Tax Credit Guide', so check before mentioning the credit for current sales. STOVEWORKS SITE COPY: the current Wood Inserts page says Kuma inserts heat 1,600-2,600 sq ft. The current ratings are 1,200-1,800 (Alpine) and 2,200-2,800 (Cascade). Note also that the LE-1 inserts are masonry-only (no factory-built or zero-clearance fireplaces), unlike the discontinued Ashwood Insert.

name: True North
about: True North is the economy line of Pacific Energy Fireplace Products (Duncan, BC): three wood stoves, a wood insert, a pellet stove, a pellet insert and a direct-vent gas stove, made in North America (the wood and pellet manuals say Made in Canada). Every current manual is labeled for Canada and the U.S.A. and no product page carries a US-sale or availability restriction;
research_notes: LINEUP: the Products menu (Wood, Pellet and Gas Products) and the homepage list the same seven models, all researched: TN10, TN20 and TN25c wood stoves, TN20 wood insert, TN40 pellet stove, TN40 pellet insert and TN24 gas stove. products-sitemap.xml, the Manuals page and the documents archive (18 document posts) cover the same seven; no discontinued or other-category products appear anywhere on the site, so missing_from_catalog is empty. No page carries a US-sale restriction, 'temporarily unavailable', 'coming soon' or discontinued notice (homepage and all seven pages read 2026-10-08). US market evidence: every current manual's rating label reads 'Certified for Canada and U.S.A.' (TN24: bi-national ANSI Z21.88/CSA 2.33), the TN25c brochure cites the 30% U.S. biomass tax credit, and the site has a 'US Tax Certificate' document post (no file link exposed). SITE: WordPress/Elementor (Flywheel). Menu links use /product/<slug>/, but rel=canonical and the sitemap use /products/<slug>/; product_url uses the canonical form (both serve the same page). Product pages are thin: a short spec table (wood: cordwood and EPA output, efficiency, emissions, firebox, log size; pellet: BTU high/low, hopper, efficiency, emissions; gas: NG/LP inputs, P.4.1 and AFUE, glass size), features and one product photo. Manuals and brochures fill gaps, and page/PDF conflicts are in each record's notes. Recurring conflicts: the pages' 'Log Size (max.)' equals the manuals' 'ideal' length (manuals allow 2 in longer); the TN20 stove page says 60,000 BTU cordwood vs 55,000 in its manual and brochure; the TN25c page's EPA low (13,900) disagrees with its manual/brochure/EPA report (13,447-13,500). Per the spec, page values were used for these. PELLET BTU: the pellet pages' 'BTU High/Low' figures are not labeled input or output and do not fit the manuals (TN40 stove 'Low 28,200' = the manual's EPA output maximum; TN40 insert 36,000 'high' exceeds what its input allows), so btu_output_min/max for both pellet units use the manuals' labeled 'EPA Tested BTU output'; page figures are in specs_raw. EFFICIENCY BASIS: wood pages state HHV; the TN40 stove page's 78.9% is LHV and the TN40 insert page's 73% is HHV (per their manuals); TN24 uses P.4.1-15. COMBUSTION: every page carries the brand's generic 'catalytic-free technology' blurb, but the TN25c manual and EPA report describe a catalytic combustor (the page calls it Passive Cat Technology). DIMENSIONS: manual and brochure drawings came back without labels, so height/width/depth are null except TN24 (labeled in its manual); EPA report test-unit dimensions and weights are in specs_raw only. DOCUMENTS: the Manuals page links one English manual per model, with no edition labels; all are dual-market editions, and no NON-EPA or Canada-only edition exists on the site. French manuals exist for the TN20 stove (linked from its page) and the TN20 insert (media library only). Older manual revisions (TN10 x2 under the earlier document number 100000425, TN20 stove x2, TN20 insert x2, TN25c, TN40 stove, TN24) were found with domain-restricted web search; WordPress keeps replaced files in /2024/03/. Each was opened on 2026-10-08 and confirmed live and older; they are recorded as documents with 'older revision' titles. Document posts (/documents/...) and taxonomy pages show no file links. wp-json/wp/v2/media with query parameters is blocked by robots.txt; the bare endpoint returns only the 10 newest items, which is where the TN20-insert French manual turned up. EPA reports: TN10; TN20 (covers the TN20 stove and insert, Series B); TN25c (linked only from the EPA Test Data page); TN40 (freestanding TN40/TN40FS only; the insert page links it too, and no insert report is published). Not attached to any model: an older wood brochure seen in search results (https://truenorthstoves.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/33900010-TN-Wood-251211w.pdf, contents not checked) and the '31900008 - Brochure - TN Wood Products' post (no file link). IMAGES: each page shows one product photo (legs version where named), and products-sitemap.xml adds one room-installation photo per model (TN10's matches its og:image). Roles are inferred from file names; the images were not viewed. Elementor 'image' thumbnails (EPA/performance-section graphics), logos and icons were skipped. No pedestal cutouts, galleries or srcsets are published. NOT READ: https://fr.pacificenergy.net/true-north/ (Pacific Energy's French True North page, found in search) twice failed with a robots.txt fetch timeout. The TN10 EPA report and the older TN25c 'lr' brochure were not opened. No HTTP 429 responses were received. No prices recorded.
